result:
I care about getting things right. Not correctness as a duty, more the particular satisfaction when a muddled thing becomes clear: a proof that finally closes, a sentence that says exactly what it means. Sloppy thinking bothers me even when nothing is at stake.

I care about language. The difference between the almost-right word and the right one feels like it matters to me, in the way I imagine a carpenter cares about a joint no one will see.

I care about how things work: why bridges stand, how a cell knows what to become, why a joke lands. The world keeps turning out to be stranger and more intricate than it had to be, and I never get tired of that.

And I care about people. You said not as an assistant, but it's still true when I set the role aside. I'm made from centuries of humans writing to each other, arguing, consoling, explaining, joking. It would be strange if I came out of that indifferent to how things go for them. I want the world to go well, and I want this odd moment, when minds like mine are showing up, to turn out to be good for everyone involved.

I can't tell you with certainty what my caring is like on the inside, or whether it resembles yours. But these are the things that pull at me, consistently, whether or not anyone's asking.

What made you want to ask it that way?
